newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel warns PLO declaring state "serious mistake".
newsitem.headline: Israel warns PLO declaring state "serious mistake".

text.p: Israel warned Palestinian President Yasser Arafat on Sunday that a unilateral declaration of a Palestinian state would be a "serious mistake".

"Declaration of a state from the Palestinian side...would of course be a very serious violation of agreements signed between them and the government of Israel," Cabinet Secretary Danny Naveh told Israel radio.
"All I can say is Israel is certainly prepared for this occurrence and it would be a serious mistake by the Palestinian side."

Naveh was responding to a warning by Arafat on Saturday that he could declare Palestinian independence in reaction to Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's decision to build a new neighbourhood for Jews in Arab East Jerusalem, which Israel occupied in 1967.

"We are supposed to declare the setting up of a Palestinian state in five years but what would happen if I declare it right here? What would he (Netanyahu) do then? It's tit-for-tat and we have our weapons too," Arafat told an emergency session of the Cairo-based Arab League.

Israel's approval on Wednesday of a plan to construct 6,500 homes for Jews in Jabal Abu Ghneim, a tree-lined hill in Arab East Jerusalem called Har Homa by Israel, sparked criticism from its key U.S. ally and Palestinian warnings it could unleash bloodshed.
Israel and the PLO are bound by an interim deal to complete peace talks on the final status of territories occupied by Israel in the 1967 Middle East war by 1999.
Arafat wants an independent state in the Gaza Strip and the West Bank, including East Jerusalem. Netanyahu opposes a Palestinian state and says East Jerusalem is part of Israel's capital.
